units.text: INT. DRIVE-IN PROJECTION BOOTH - NIGHT
Dust in the beam.
A dead reel clatters on its spindle.
The screen outside shows only white.
NELL ASHBY (20s, headlamp, flannel) crouches at the old projector, one hand on the take-up arm, the other jamming a flathead into the gate.
A walkie-talkie sits on the splice table, crackling.
Nell? You up there? Film's gone.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I know. I'm fixing it.
units.name: NELL

units.text: No. I mean the picture's gone. The screen's... something's moving on it.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Nell freezes.
Turns her head toward the small square window.
Through the glass, the white screen ripples like a bedsheet with someone under it.
She grabs the walkie, thumbs it.

Teddy, down in the lot, stumbles backward over a speaker post, drops his flashlight, scrambles for it, and the beam swings up the length of the screen where a long grey hand presses outward from the fabric, fingers spreading, as Nell reaches back and kills the lamp, and the booth goes black except for the light slowly dying on the walls.
Teddy. Teddy, go home.
units.name: NELL

units.text: It's okay. It stopped.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Silence.
The hand on the screen is gone.
The screen is white again, perfectly flat.
That's worse.
units.name: NELL
